hunks.sol: Everything was ready. Once I left the training hall, I would gather the things I had in mind and leave the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

hunks.sol: Just dealing with dim-witted bandits like the Heavenly Axe should let me reach my target quickly. Two days at most. After that, I could return to my family’s warm embrace.

hunks.baseline: That was when the rims of my eyes started to go red.
hunks.sol: My eyes were just beginning to redden when—

hunks.baseline: This was the moment I had been waiting for. The iron door blocking the entrance to the training hall was opening. That ugly, heavy chunk of metal looked as beautiful as the gates of heaven.
hunks.sol: The moment I had been waiting for had finally arrived. The iron door blocking the entrance to the training hall was opening. That ugly, heavy chunk of metal looked as beautiful as the gates of heaven.

hunks.baseline: I ran toward the entrance to heaven with a face full of joy.
hunks.sol: Overjoyed, I raced toward the entrance to heaven.

hunks.baseline: “You will be leaving. But there’s somewhere we need to stop by first.”
hunks.sol: “You will be leaving. But there’s somewhere we need to stop first.”

hunks.baseline: “Somewhere we need to stop by?”
hunks.sol: “Somewhere we need to stop?”

hunks.baseline: A chill ran down my spine. Some kind of survival instinct raised its head.
hunks.sol: A chill ran down my spine. Some unknown survival instinct reared its head.

hunks.baseline: “Senior members of our family and an envoy from the Mount Heng Sword Sect have also arrived.”
hunks.sol: “Senior members of our family and an envoy from the Mount Heng Sword Sect are also there.”

hunks.baseline: Wolhwa had told me at Honghwaru. The Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect were sworn enemies. So why were those bastards here?
hunks.sol: Wolhwa had told me at Honghwaru that the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect were sworn enemies. So why were those bastards here?

hunks.baseline: This was ominous. Very ominous. I had to find some kind of way out of this.
hunks.sol: This was ominous. Very ominous. I had to find some way out of this.

hunks.baseline: “It seems like an important occasion, and I can’t show up smelling like this…”
hunks.sol: “This sounds like an important occasion, and I shouldn’t show up smelling like this…”

hunks.baseline: His voice was dry, and his eyes were cold. The aura coming from him made it impossible for me to open my mouth. All I could do was nod.
hunks.sol: His voice was dry, and his eyes were cold. The aura emanating from him made it impossible for me to speak. All I could do was nod.

hunks.baseline: There was no doubt about it. This bastard was responsible. He had dumped a load of shit without me even knowing.
hunks.sol: There was no doubt about it. That bastard was responsible. He had taken a shit I knew nothing about.

hunks.baseline: On the way to the main assembly hall behind Wipeng, my mind was completely blank.
hunks.sol: As I followed Wipeng toward the main assembly hall, my mind went completely blank.

hunks.baseline: Even if it had ended at an attempt, it was a sex crime so vile that beating the culprit to death wouldn’t have been enough.
hunks.sol: Even if it had only been an attempt, it was a sex crime so vile that beating the culprit to death wouldn’t have been enough.

hunks.baseline: I remembered how I had always said that, as a human being and an older brother with a younger sister, sex offenders should be executed.
hunks.sol: As a human being and an older brother with a younger sister, I had always said that sex offenders deserved to be executed.

hunks.baseline: *What kind of fucking lunatic was he?*
hunks.sol: *That crazy son of a bitch.*

hunks.baseline: My palms were damp with cold sweat. I said it again, not knowing how many times I had repeated it already.
hunks.sol: My palms were slick with cold sweat. For what had to be the hundredth time, I said,

hunks.baseline: “I really wasn’t the one. Please believe me.”
hunks.sol: “It really wasn’t me. Please believe me.”

hunks.baseline: “No, that’s not what I mean. I’m telling you, it really wasn’t me. Do I look like the kind of guy who’d do that? The kind of guy who’d go around committing trash like that?”
hunks.sol: “No, that’s not what I mean. I’m telling you, it really wasn’t me. Do I look like the kind of guy who’d do that? Like someone who’d go around doing something that disgusting?”

hunks.baseline: “Just go here.”
hunks.sol: “Then relieve yourself here.”

hunks.baseline: Son of a bitch. I gave up and immediately turned around and ran, drawing up all my internal energy and concentrating it in my feet.
hunks.sol: Son of a bitch. I gave up and immediately turned and ran, drawing up all my internal energy and concentrating it in my feet.

hunks.baseline: I was caught in three steps. Wipeng had me by the back of the neck, looking down at me with cold eyes.
hunks.sol: I was caught in three steps. Wipeng had me by the back of the neck and was looking down at me with cold eyes.

hunks.baseline: “If you keep this up… I might have to stop being polite.”
hunks.sol: “If you keep this up… I may have to stop being polite.”

hunks.baseline: With a sinking heart, I walked for who knew how long before a tall pavilion came into view.
hunks.sol: I trudged on with a sinking heart. After what felt like an eternity, a tall pavilion came into view.

hunks.baseline: Several warriors were standing guard outside. I recognized the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s distinctive navy uniforms, but some of the men wore red clothes I had never seen before.
hunks.sol: Several warriors stood guard outside. I recognized the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s distinctive navy uniforms, but some of the men wore red clothes I had never seen before.

hunks.baseline: Considering the usual relationship between the two sects, they should have been sworn enemies. Yet right now, they were united in glaring at me.
hunks.sol: Considering the usual relationship between the two sides, they should have been at each other’s throats. Yet right now, they were united in glaring at me.

hunks.baseline: I took a deep breath and stepped into the pavilion. Inside my head, I kept repeating the same words.
hunks.sol: I took a deep breath and stepped into the pavilion, repeating the same words over and over in my head.

hunks.baseline: The moment I entered the hall, the low murmuring abruptly stopped. A dozen men, young and old, stood arrayed along either side, while Jin Wikyung occupied the seat of honor.
hunks.sol: The moment I entered the hall, the low murmurs abruptly stopped. A dozen men, young and old, stood arrayed along either side, while Jin Wikyung occupied the seat of honor.

hunks.baseline: The instant I met that unpleasant smile—
hunks.sol: The instant I saw his unpleasant smile—

hunks.sol: …At least signal before you cut in.

hunks.sol: If I had to compare it to something, it was like the difference between a low-level monster and a mid-level monster. His killing intent was far more refined, subtle, and chilling.

hunks.baseline: Each word was spat out by Lee Seogeun. Above his head, a System window floated in the air.
hunks.sol: Lee Seogeun bit off each word. Above his head, a System window floated in the air.

hunks.baseline: That was the Level I had seen with Qi Sense the instant I detected his killing intent. It was more than twice my Level.
hunks.sol: That was the Level I had read with Qi Sense the instant I detected his killing intent. It was more than twice my Level.

hunks.baseline: Dozens of sinister gazes, young and old alike, were fixed on me. My knees began to tremble. In that atmosphere, Lee Seogeun opened his mouth.
hunks.sol: Dozens of menacing eyes, young and old alike, were fixed on me. My knees began to weaken. Amid that atmosphere, Lee Seogeun spoke.

hunks.baseline: “What a shame. If you had come a little earlier, we could have had a deeper conversation. We were discussing something interesting until just now.”
hunks.sol: “What a shame. If you had arrived a little earlier, we could have had a deeper conversation. We were discussing something interesting until just now.”

hunks.baseline: I only hoped it wasn’t a discussion about whether to cut off my head or my balls. And if that miserable guess was correct, I preferred them to cut off my balls instead of my head.
hunks.sol: I only hoped it wasn’t a discussion about whether to cut off my head or my balls. And if that miserable guess was correct, I would rather they cut off my balls than my head.

hunks.baseline: *I might be able to recover with a Level Up if they did that… Why am I even thinking about this?*
hunks.sol: *If I’m lucky, a Level Up might heal them… Why am I even thinking about this?*

hunks.baseline: It was simply miserable. Lee Seogeun studied my expression before speaking again.
hunks.sol: It was beyond miserable. Lee Seogeun studied my expression before speaking again.

hunks.baseline: “I heard you returned to the family a few days ago. Where have you been?”
hunks.sol: “I heard you returned to the family a few days ago. Where were you?”

hunks.sol: *I got fired from my Guild that day, shared some soju with the older guy from my goshiwon, then climbed into the capsule and fell asleep. When I woke up, I was at Honghwaru, and now I’m working hard toward Logout. Something like that.*

hunks.baseline: *It’d be a miracle if he didn’t draw his sword.*
hunks.sol: *I’d be lucky if he didn’t draw his sword.*

hunks.sol: “The pleasure house you used to frequent? Don’t try to claim you’ve never heard of it. I have the testimony and signatures of the people who saw you there that day.”

hunks.sol: In other words, it was a list of witness statements. Figuring I might as well look, I read through the papers.

hunks.baseline: “You don’t know even after seeing it yourself?”
hunks.sol: “You can’t tell even after reading it?”

hunks.baseline: “I’m saying that because I read it. There isn’t a single proper testimony here.”
hunks.sol: “I’m asking because I read it. There isn’t a single proper statement here.”

hunks.sol: I read every one of the dozens of statements, but not one contained anything decisive.

hunks.baseline: They all said roughly the same thing: Jin Taekyung had gotten thoroughly drunk, gone to the wrong room, and found that the room belonged to the daughter of the Mount Heng Sword Sect. Then someone had heard screaming.
hunks.sol: They all said roughly the same thing: Jin Taekyung had gotten thoroughly drunk, gone to the wrong room, and that room had belonged to the daughter of the Mount Heng Sword Sect. Then someone had heard a scream.

hunks.baseline: Flutter!
hunks.sol: Fwap!

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t irritation. I was simply suspicious.
hunks.sol: I wasn’t annoyed. Just suspicious.

hunks.sol: How should I put it? This whole chain of events—especially the witness statements—felt incredibly contrived.

hunks.sol: “Come outside, you bastard! I’ll make you pay for what you’ve done!”
